Print `n!` exactly. 1000! has 2568 digits, so store the number as a dynamic array of digits that **grows with `realloc`** whenever a carry needs another digit.

**Input:** `n`.

**Output:** the number of digits of `n!`, then `n!` itself.

**Constraints:** 0 ≤ n ≤ 2000

## Hints

1. Keep digits least-significant first: `d[0]` is the units digit. Start with one digit, `1`.
2. To multiply by `k`: for each digit, `cur = d[i] * k + carry; d[i] = cur % 10; carry = cur / 10;`. Then, while `carry > 0`, append `carry % 10` (growing the array if full) and divide `carry` by 10.

```c starter
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

int main(void) {
    int n;
    scanf("%d", &n);
    size_t len = 1, cap = 16;
    unsigned char *d = malloc(cap);
    d[0] = 1;
    /* multiply by 2..n, growing as needed */
    free(d);
    return 0;
}
```

```c solution
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

int main(void) {
    int n;
    if (scanf("%d", &n) != 1) return 1;
    size_t len = 1, cap = 16;
    unsigned char *d = malloc(cap);
    if (!d) return 1;
    d[0] = 1;
    for (int k = 2; k <= n; k++) {
        int carry = 0;
        for (size_t i = 0; i < len; i++) {
            int cur = d[i] * k + carry;
            d[i] = (unsigned char)(cur % 10);
            carry = cur / 10;
        }
        while (carry) {
            if (len == cap) {
                unsigned char *t = realloc(d, cap *= 2);
                if (!t) { free(d); return 1; }
                d = t;
            }
            d[len++] = (unsigned char)(carry % 10);
            carry /= 10;
        }
    }
    printf("%zu\n", len);
    for (size_t i = len; i-- > 0;) putchar('0' + d[i]);
    putchar('\n');
    free(d);
    return 0;
}
```
